newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-monitors find Romania poll "reasonably fair".
newsitem.headline: Euro-monitors find Romania poll "reasonably fair".

text.p: Council of Europe election monitors found the first round of voting in Romanian presidential and legislative elections earlier this month to be free and "reasonably fair", the council said on Tuesday.

The delegation from the council's parliamentary assembly "unanimously agreed that the 3 November elections were free, reasonably fair and transparent, despite minor irregularities resulting from technical administration of the voting and application of electoral legislation", the council said.

Delegation officials said the biggest problems were related to the updating of the permanent voters' list and the verification of special voters' lists, which in some polling stations represented as many as 20 percent of voters.
The council was set up after World War Two to foster democracy and human rights across Europe.
The second round of voting in Romania is set for Sunday. President Ion Iliescu, seeking re-election after seven years in power, is being challenged by centrist Emil Constantinescu.
Iliescu finished four percentage points ahead of Constantinescu in the first round of voting.

But in parliamentary elections, Iliescu's PDSR was trounced by the CDR, pushing his party out of government for the first time in the post-communist era though Iliescu and most members of the outgoing government created a safety net for themselves by winning parliamentary seats.
